# Social Migration Studio

The Awtsmoos renews remembered social vessels without pretending their history was born here;
Awtsmoos.com keeps archive opening local, planning dry, selected upload explicit, and publication causally clear.

## Purpose

`/social/migrate/` imports authored Facebook and Instagram history and links to advanced YouTube migration. Choosing a ZIP, folder, JSON file, or HTML file does not upload it. The browser inspects metadata locally and uploads only media required by explicitly selected memories after import begins.

## Facebook and Instagram exports

Use Accounts Center → Your information and permissions → Export your information → Create export. Choose the profile, export to device, select the wanted content/date range/format/media quality, and prefer All time + JSON for the fullest structured migration. Open the resulting ZIP, extracted folder, JSON, or older HTML export in `/social/migrate/`.

Official Facebook export help: https://www.facebook.com/help/212802592074644
Official Instagram export help: https://www.facebook.com/help/181231772500920

## YouTube exports

For a whole creator archive, use Google Takeout, select YouTube and YouTube Music, choose the wanted YouTube data, create a one-time ZIP export, download every part, then use `/youtube/migrate/`.

Google Takeout help: https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/3024190?hl=en
Google Takeout: https://takeout.google.com/

For one owned video, use YouTube Studio → Content → video menu → Download, then bring the media and metadata into the advanced migration workflow.

YouTube Studio help: https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/56100?hl=en
YouTube Studio: https://studio.youtube.com/

## Local-first archive safety

ZIP opening reads the central directory first instead of inflating every media file. JSON is preferred while HTML remains supported for older exports. Imported HTML is neutralized before detached parsing: executable containers and event handlers are removed and fetch-capable resource attributes become inert data. Archive paths reject traversal, absolute paths, URI schemes, Windows drive escapes, and NUL bytes. Unknown source dates stay Unknown rather than becoming the Unix epoch.

## Review and import flow

1. Open the archive locally and inspect detected provider evidence.
2. Filter/select memories and choose Alias, Heichel, and Series.
3. Run server preflight and generate a dry plan.
4. Explicitly begin import.
5. Upload only selected image/video/audio media.
6. Preserve returned native asset manifests.
7. Re-plan with the real `publicPath` values.
8. Publish through `/api/social/unified-social/publish`.
9. Save checkpoint evidence and retry unfinished work without duplicating completed idempotency keys.

## API and provenance truth

The browser negotiates migration limits from the server. Capability discovery, preflight, dry planning, asset upload, and publication are separate gates. `API.md` documents routes, response semantics, native assets, and retry/idempotency rules.

Imported reaction/comment/share counts remain historical provenance. Imported comments never become fake native Awtsmoos user comments. Provenance can preserve provider, source ID/URL/type/profile, known publication date, archive path, media paths, historical counts, and import time.

## Recovery

The local checkpoint stores serializable evidence only: selected IDs, destination, returned native asset manifests, completed publication IDs/idempotency evidence, failures, and timestamp. It never stores `File` objects or object URLs. After a browser restart the archive must be opened again because local file handles are not silently persisted.
